description: Covers foundational cloud concepts including the definition of cloud computing, value proposition, shared responsibility model, global infrastructure, and types of cloud deployment models. Introduces IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, elasticity, pay-as-you-go pricing, and basic AWS terminology.
usecase: Used as a baseline for all cloud learners to understand how cloud computing changes infrastructure operations, business agility, cost models, and scaling strategies.
additionalInfo: Deployment models: public, private, hybrid cloud.
Cloud advantages: agility, on-demand provisioning, elasticity, cost optimization, resiliency.
AWS global infrastructure: regions, availability zones, edge locations.
Shared Responsibility Model: AWS manages the cloud, customers secure configurations.
Cloud economics: OpEx vs CapEx, right-sizing, consumption-based pricing.

description: Overview of compute concepts like virtual machines, containers, serverless computing, autoscaling, availability, and elasticity. Explains how compute resources are provisioned and managed in AWS.
usecase: Foundation for understanding compute services such as EC2, Autoscaling, container services, and serverless runtimes.
additionalInfo: Compute models: virtual machines, containerized workloads, serverless functions.
Workload types: stateful vs stateless, batch vs real-time, event-driven.
Elasticity: automatic scale-out and scale-in to meet traffic demands.
Cost drivers: instance type, usage hours, storage attached, data transfer.

description: Virtual servers in the cloud offering flexible compute capacity with full control over OS, networking, and software environment. Supports a variety of instance families optimized for general purpose, compute, memory, storage, and GPU workloads.
usecase: Hosting web servers, application backends, batch processing, GPU workloads, enterprise applications, legacy server migrations.
additionalInfo: Instance types: t-series, m-series, r-series, c-series, p/g-series for GPUs.
Storage: EBS volumes, instance store, shared file systems.
Scaling: EC2 Auto Scaling, Launch Templates, Spot instances.
Networking: security groups, ENIs, VPC placement.
Pricing models: On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, Spot.

description: Deep dive into AWS compute offerings including AWS Lambda, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, AWS Fargate, and Lightsail. Covers orchestration, event-driven compute, container registries, and microservices patterns.
usecase: Selecting the appropriate compute service for microservices, containers, event-driven systems, serverless APIs, and lightweight deployments.
additionalInfo: Serverless: AWS Lambda for event-driven compute.
Container orchestration: ECS (AWS-native), EKS (Kubernetes).
Execution models: Fargate (serverless containers) vs EC2-backed nodes.
Container registry: Amazon ECR for image storage.
Use cases: microservices, CI/CD pipelines, data processing.

description: Explains AWS’s global footprint, multi-region architecture, high availability design, latency optimization, and content delivery using Amazon CloudFront and global networking services.
usecase: Architecting resilient, low-latency applications deployed across multiple regions or globally distributed user bases.
additionalInfo: AWS Global Infrastructure: Regions, AZs, Local Zones, Wavelength.
Content Delivery: Amazon CloudFront for caching and edge compute.
Latency optimization: Route 53 routing policies.
Disaster recovery strategies: backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby, multi-site active/active.
Data residency & compliance considerations.

description: Covers VPC fundamentals, subnets, routing, security groups, NAT gateways, Direct Connect, VPN, load balancing, and network security principles. Explains hybrid cloud architecture.
usecase: Design secure network boundaries, connect on-premises environments, build scalable web applications, and control traffic flow using AWS networking resources.
additionalInfo: VPC components: IGW, NAT, route tables, NACLs.
Load balancing: ALB, NLB, Gateway Load Balancer.
Connectivity: Direct Connect, Site-to-Site VPN, Transit Gateway.
Security layers: WAF, Shield, security groups vs NACLs.
Networking patterns: hub-and-spoke, multi-VPC, hybrid networks.

description: Overview of cloud storage types including object storage, block storage, file storage, archival storage, backup, and data transfer capabilities. Explains durability, availability, and lifecycle policies.
usecase: Selecting the best storage type for applications such as backups, content hosting, shared file storage, databases, media streaming, and big data workloads.
additionalInfo: Object Storage: Amazon S3 (buckets, lifecycle rules, versioning).
Block Storage: EBS for low-latency, high-performance workloads.
File Storage: EFS for Linux and FSx for Windows/Lustre.
Archival: S3 Glacier and Glacier Deep Archive.
Data transfer: Snowball, DataSync, Transfer Family.

description: Overview of database concepts, categories, and how database services are offered and consumed in the cloud. Covers relational and non-relational models, transactional vs analytical workloads, OLTP vs OLAP, consistency models, scaling approaches, and managed database tradeoffs.
usecase: Central reference for choosing, architecting, securing, operating, and scaling database services for applications (web/mobile backends, analytics pipelines, caching layers, graph workloads, time-series, backups and disaster recovery).
additionalInfo: Core Concepts: schemas, tables/collections, indexes, ACID, BASE, partitioning/sharding, replication, failover, backups, point-in-time recovery (PITR).
Operational Concerns: provisioning, monitoring, patching, maintenance windows, scaling (vertical vs horizontal), cost drivers (storage, IOPS, backup, data transfer).
Integration: connectors, ORMs, SDKs, data migration tools (e.g., DMS), event-driven DB integrations (Streams/Change Data Capture).
Architectural Patterns: single-master vs multi-master, read replicas, cache-aside, write-through, CQRS, event sourcing, data lakes vs operational stores.
Compliance & Governance: encryption at rest/in transit, audit logging, access control, retention policies, backups and cross-region replication.

description: Structured data stores that use schemas (tables, columns, types) and SQL for queries. Provide strong consistency, transactions (ACID), complex queries and joins, indexing, and mature tooling for data integrity.
usecase: Transactional systems (banking, e-commerce), business applications, systems that need joins and relational integrity, OLTP workloads, reporting with normalized schemas.
additionalInfo: Common engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle (managed or self-managed).
Scaling approaches: vertical scaling (bigger instance), read replicas for read scaling, partitioning/partition pruning for large datasets.
Operational features to consider: automated backups, PITR, maintenance windows, major/minor patch management.
Design best practices: normalize where appropriate, index selectively, avoid unbounded scans, use prepared statements/parameterized queries.

description: Databases that provide flexible schemas or schema-less storage, optimized for scale, high throughput and availability. Includes key-value, document, wide-column, and graph models with diverse consistency and query capabilities.
usecase: High-scale web/mobile backends, session stores, user profiles, IoT time-series ingestion, content catalogs, semi-structured data, graph workloads.
additionalInfo: Types: key-value stores, document stores (JSON), column-family stores, graph databases, time-series DBs.
Design principle: model data around access patterns (denormalization often required).
Consistency models: eventual, strong (depends on service), tunable consistency in some systems.
Tradeoffs: simplicity and scale vs weaker relational features (no multi-table transactions or complex joins in many cases).

description: Managed relational database service that automates provisioning, patching, backup, recovery, and scaling for engines such as Amazon Aurora, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, and SQL Server.
usecase: Easily run production-grade relational databases with reduced operational overhead: transactional applications, ERP, CRM, and legacy app migrations.
additionalInfo: Key features: automated backups, snapshots, Multi-AZ deployments for high availability, read replicas (where supported), monitoring via CloudWatch, integration with IAM and KMS.
Engines supported: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, Aurora (as a specialized engine).
Scaling: scale compute/storage vertically, read replicas for horizontal read scaling; storage autoscaling available.
Maintenance: automated minor version upgrades; user-controlled maintenance windows for major events.
Networking & Security: VPC placement, subnet groups, security groups, encryption at rest using AWS KMS, encryption in transit (TLS).
Backups & DR: Automated snapshots and manual snapshots; cross-region snapshot copy for disaster recovery planning.
Common integrations: DMS (Database Migration Service) for migrations, CloudWatch for metrics, Event Notifications for lifecycle events.
Limitations & considerations: instance class and IOPS influence cost and performance; some engines have licensing considerations (Oracle, SQL Server).

description: High-performance managed relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, designed for the cloud with a distributed, fault-tolerant storage architecture and automated scaling of storage.
usecase: Applications that need high throughput and low-latency relational storage with managed HA: SaaS multi-tenant backends, e-commerce, analytics-backed transactional apps.
additionalInfo: Architecture: decoupled compute and distributed storage replicating across multiple AZs with fast crash recovery and continuous backup to S3.
Performance: often offers better throughput than vanilla MySQL/Postgres on equivalent hardware due to storage and engine optimizations.
Scaling: read replicas (Aurora Replicas) with fast failover; serverless option (Aurora Serverless v2) for variable workloads.
High availability: built-in fault isolation, automated failover, and cross-region read replicas for geo-distribution.
Operational features: backtrack (time-travel for small rollbacks), automated backups, snapshots, Global Database for cross-region read scaling and disaster recovery.
Security: supports encryption at rest (KMS), in-transit TLS, IAM authentication, VPC and security groups.
Cost drivers: instance hours, storage consumed, I/O operations, backup storage and data transfer for cross-region replication.
Migration: supports native engine migration paths and AWS DMS for lift-and-shift.

description: Fully managed key-value and document database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. Provides serverless operation, automatic partitioning, and optional DynamoDB Streams for change data capture.
usecase: High-scale web apps, leaderboards, session stores, mobile backends, IoT telemetry ingestion, ad-tech, and any workload requiring predictable low latency at scale.
additionalInfo: Data model: items (rows) and attributes (columns) stored in tables; primary keys can be simple or composite; secondary indexes enable alternate access patterns.
Capacity modes: provisioned capacity (with autoscaling) and on-demand capacity (pay-per-request).
Scaling & performance: automatic sharding/partitioning, DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator) for microsecond caching, adaptive capacity for uneven workloads.
Consistency: supports eventually consistent and strongly consistent reads (strong reads cost more/are region-limited).
Durability & availability: multi-AZ replication by default; global tables for multi-region active-active replication.
Integrations: Streams for CDC, Lambda triggers, IAM policies, CloudWatch metrics, backups & restores, TTL for data lifecycle management.
Security: encryption at rest (KMS), VPC endpoints (PrivateLink), fine-grained access control (IAM policies and condition keys), PITR (Point-in-time recovery).
Design best practices: model for access patterns, avoid hot partitions, use adaptive capacity, consider GSIs/LSIs wisely, batch operations for efficiency.

description: Caching layers that store frequently accessed data in memory to reduce latency and lower load on primary databases. Provide sub-millisecond access and are used to accelerate read-heavy workloads.
usecase: Session stores, leaderboard counters, frequently-read configuration or metadata, computed results, short-lived tokens, and to reduce database read pressure.
additionalInfo: Models: cache-aside (application controls cache lifecycle), write-through, write-back, and read-through patterns.
Tradeoffs: caches improve latency but introduce cache consistency complexity; decide TTL and eviction policies carefully.
Common capabilities: data eviction (LRU/LFU), persistence options in some products, clustering/sharding for scale, and replication for HA.
Operational concerns: eviction storms, cache warming, cold-start behavior, monitoring hit/miss ratios, and accounting for eventual consistency.

description: Managed, in-memory caching service supporting Redis and Memcached engines. Automates cluster provisioning, patching, backups (Redis), failure detection and recovery.
usecase: Accelerate application performance through caching, implement pub/sub workflows (Redis), session storage, real-time analytics, and leaderboard or counters.
additionalInfo: Supported engines: Redis (persistence options, replication, clustering) and Memcached (simple distributed cache).
Redis features: persistence (RDB/AOF), replication with automatic failover, clustering for horizontal scaling, modules (when supported), Lua scripting.
Deployment options: single-node, clusters with shards, Multi-AZ (Redis) for high availability.
Security: VPC-only access, security groups, in-transit encryption (TLS) and at-rest encryption for Redis (when enabled), IAM integration via service roles for management.
Operational best practices: size nodes for working set, monitor key metrics (CPU, memory, evictions, replication lag), use backup/restore for Redis persistence, test failover scenarios.
Cost model: instance hours, data transfer, snapshots (for Redis), and cluster topology.

description: Managed document database service compatible with MongoDB workloads. Designed for JSON-like document storage, indexing, and querying with managed storage, backup, and scaling.
usecase: Content management, user profiles, catalogs, and any workload that benefits from document model flexibility and MongoDB-compatible drivers.
additionalInfo: Compatibility: supports many MongoDB APIs and drivers—validate version compatibility for driver-specific features.
Architecture: separation of compute and distributed storage; replicas for read scaling.
Operational capabilities: automated backups, snapshots, point-in-time restore, monitoring, and Multi-AZ deployments.
Limitations to check: ensure feature parity for advanced MongoDB features (some server-side modules or specific commands may not be supported).
Security: VPC, IAM integration for management, encryption at rest via KMS, TLS for in-transit encryption.

description: Managed graph database service optimized for storing and querying highly-connected datasets, with support for property graph (Gremlin) and RDF/SPARQL models.
usecase: Knowledge graphs, fraud detection, social networks, recommendation engines, network/IT topology analysis.
additionalInfo: Data models: property graphs (TinkerPop/Gremlin) and RDF with SPARQL querying—choose based on application requirements.
Performance: optimized for graph traversals and queries that would be inefficient in relational or document stores.
High availability: Multi-AZ, automated backups, read replicas for read scaling.
Security: VPC-only access, IAM control for management plane operations, encryption at rest (KMS) and in transit (TLS).
Integrations: can be integrated with analytics pipelines, ML workflows and visualization tools for graph-analysis.

description: Centralized backup service that automates and consolidates backup of AWS services (including RDS, DynamoDB, EBS, EFS, and on-premises via Gateway) with policy-based scheduling and retention.
usecase: Implement organization-wide backup policies, retention schedules, compliance archiving, and recoverability across multiple AWS services including relational and non-relational databases.
additionalInfo: Capabilities: centralized policy management, lifecycle (move to cold storage), cross-account and cross-region backup copy for DR, backup activity logging.
Supported DBs: RDS (including Aurora), DynamoDB (on-demand backups and PITR), DocumentDB (via snapshots/backup features), and others depending on AWS updates.
Disaster recovery: use cross-region copies and vaults with distinct access controls for recovery objectives.
Security & compliance: encryption of backups, IAM-based controls over backup vaults, and audit via CloudTrail.
Operational notes: coordinate backup windows with database maintenance and consider backup impact on performance.

description: Security considerations, controls, and best practices specific to databases: authentication, authorization, encryption, network controls, monitoring, auditing, and data governance.
usecase: Protect sensitive data, meet compliance requirements (e.g., GDPR, PCI, HIPAA), prevent unauthorized access and data leakage, and enable secure operations.
additionalInfo: Authentication & Authorization: use IAM for management plane operations, database-native auth for connections, and role-based access controls; enable least-privilege.
Encryption: enable encryption at rest (KMS-managed keys) and in-transit (TLS). Use customer-managed keys for separation of duties where required.
Network Controls: place DBs in private subnets, restrict access with security groups and network ACLs, use VPC endpoints/PrivateLink to avoid public internet exposure.
Secrets Management: store DB credentials and rotation policies in a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager) and avoid hard-coding credentials.
Auditing & Monitoring: enable audit logging (e.g., RDS enhanced monitoring, CloudTrail, database audit logs), set up SIEM ingestion and alerts for suspicious activity.
Backup Security: secure backup storage with encryption and access policies, verify restore procedures as part of compliance audits.
Data Protection: use masking, tokenization, or field-level encryption for PII; apply retention and deletion policies per regulations.
Operational Hardening: minimize surface area (close unused ports, disable unused features), prompt patching, periodic vulnerability scans and penetration testing.
Incident Response: run recovery drills, maintain runbooks for compromised credentials, and automate revocation and rotation procedures.

description: Practical guidance and runbook-style items for designing schemas, capacity planning, monitoring, backups, and incident response for database services in production.
usecase: Provide teams with actionable checklists and patterns to reduce outage risk, improve performance, and ensure recoverability.
additionalInfo: Design checks: model for access patterns, choose indexes for query plans, avoid wide columns and unbounded list attributes, set appropriate fill factors and maintenance tasks.
Capacity planning: test under load, use representative datasets for benchmarking, plan IOPS and network throughput, enable autoscaling where supported.
Observability: monitor latency, throughput, replica lag, CPU, memory, disk usage, connection counts, cache hit ratios and slow query logs; create dashboards & alerts.
Backups & DR: define RTO/RPO, configure automated backups and PITR, validate periodic restores to non-prod environments, keep cross-region copies if required.
Maintenance: schedule rolling upgrades where available, test engine version upgrades in staging, use parameter groups templates under IaC.
Runbooks: document steps for failover, promote read-replica, restore from snapshot, rotate credentials, and escalate to vendor or cloud support.
Cost optimization: right-size instances, use reserved or saving plans for predictable workloads, remove unused replicas and snapshots periodically.
Automation & IaC: provision DBs and parameter groups via Infrastructure as Code, use CI for schema migrations and migrations tools with rollback strategies.

description: Approaches and tools for migrating databases to the cloud or between engines (lift-and-shift, replatform, refactor) including strategies for minimal downtime and data validation.
usecase: Migrate on-prem databases to managed cloud databases, modernize legacy systems (e.g., move from monolith to microservices with different persistence), perform homogeneous and heterogeneous migrations.
additionalInfo: Common tools: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) for continuous replication, native export/import, logical replication, and offline snapshot methods.
Patterns: cutover (small downtime), blue/green (parallel run with switch), phased migration (per service or table), dual-write with eventual sync (careful with desync).
Pre-migration checklist: assess schema compatibility, reserved words, stored procedures, triggers, data type differences, and performance characteristics (indexes, queries).
Testing: run integrity checks, compare row counts, perform reconciliation with checksums, conduct performance and failover tests in staging.
Post-migration: decommission old systems, update runbooks, finalize cutover date, set up monitoring and alerts, and train operations teams.

fullName: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning & Data Analytics
description: Covers AWS AI/ML services, big data processing, analytics platforms, and data lake solutions. Explains managed ML workflows and serverless analytics using AWS native tools.
usecase: Building ML applications, performing business analytics, running distributed ETL workflows, training ML models, and deploying intelligent services.
additionalInfo: AI Services: Rekognition, Comprehend, Polly, Lex, Transcribe, Translate.
ML Services: Amazon SageMaker (studio, training, inference).
Analytics: Athena (SQL on S3), Glue ETL, EMR, Kinesis, MSK.
Data Lakes: Lake Formation + S3.
Processing engines: Spark, Presto, Flink, Hadoop.

description: Covers identity and access management, data protection, AWS security services, and best practices for securing cloud resources following the shared responsibility model.
usecase: Designing secure applications, enforcing least-privilege, encrypting data, monitoring for threats, and meeting compliance obligations.
additionalInfo: Identity: IAM, SSO, Organizations, Access Analyzer.
Detection: GuardDuty, Security Hub, Inspector, Detective.
Protection: KMS, Secrets Manager, WAF, Shield.
Governance: SCPs, audit logs, CloudTrail.
Best practices: least-privilege, MFA, zero-trust, encryption everywhere.

module: X. Monitoring, Compliance, Governance in AWS Cloud
description: Explains AWS observability tools, audit and compliance frameworks, monitoring strategies, and governance controls to enforce organizational policies.
usecase: Implementing centralized monitoring, enforcing compliance, setting guardrails, collecting logs, and auditing resource configurations.
additionalInfo: Monitoring: CloudWatch metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards.
Audit: CloudTrail events, Access Analyzer.
Configuration: AWS Config rules, conformance packs.
Compliance: Artifact, security frameworks (SOC, PCI, HIPAA).
Governance: Control Tower, Service Catalog, tagging strategies.

description: Covers AWS cost structure, calculators, billing tools, cost management, and support tiers. Explains different pricing models across compute, storage, and database services.
usecase: Optimizing cost, budgeting, selecting support level, and controlling cloud spend for enterprise environments.
additionalInfo: Pricing models: on-demand, reserved, spot, savings plans.
Cost management: Cost Explorer, Budgets, Cost & Usage Reports.
Optimization: rightsizing, autoscaling, lifecycle policies.
Support tiers: Basic, Developer, Business, Enterprise.
Tools: Pricing Calculator, Trusted Advisor.

module: XII. Migrating to the AWS Cloud
description: Explains cloud migration strategies, tools, and frameworks including rehost, replatform, refactor, and data migration. Covers MAP (Migration Acceleration Program).
usecase: Moving on-prem workloads, datacenter exit strategies, database migration, application modernization, hybrid architectures.
additionalInfo: Migration strategies: 6 R’s (Rehost, Replatform, Repurchase, Refactor, Retire, Retain).
Tools: AWS DMS, SMS, Snowball, Application Migration Service.
Discovery: Migration Hub, data collection agents.
Modernization: microservices, serverless adoption.
Operations: cutover planning, testing, validation.

description: Covers the six pillars of AWS Well-Architected design: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability. Provides guidance on building secure, high-performing, resilient, and efficient cloud systems.
usecase: Reviewing architectures, improving system reliability, identifying risks, optimizing cost and performance, designing enterprise-grade cloud workloads.
additionalInfo: Pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.
Reviews: architectural assessments, remediation plans.
Tools: Well-Architected Tool in AWS Console.
Design patterns: multi-AZ, automation, observability, decoupling.
Operational goals: resilience, scalability, cost savings.
